passages.text: When Rachel saw that she was not bearing any children for Jacob, she envied her sister. “Give me children, or I will die!” she said to Jacob.
passages.sermon:
Rachel was Jacob’s wife.
Rachel could not have children for Jacob.
Rachel saw this.
Rachel felt envy toward her sister.
Rachel spoke to Jacob.
Rachel said, “Give me children.”
Rachel said, “If I do not have children, I will die.”
passages.original: וַתֵּ֣רֶא רָחֵ֗ל כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יָֽלְדָה֙ לְיַעֲקֹ֔ב וַתְּקַנֵּ֥א רָחֵ֖ל בַּאֲחֹתָ֑הּ וַתֹּ֤אמֶר אֶֽל־ יַעֲקֹב֙ הָֽבָה־ לִּ֣י בָנִ֔ים וְאִם־ אַ֖יִן מֵתָ֥ה אָנֹֽכִי׃

passages.text: Jacob became angry with Rachel and said, “Am I in the place of God, who has withheld children from you?”
passages.sermon:
Jacob was Rachel’s husband.
Rachel wanted children but could not have any.
Jacob became angry with Rachel.
Jacob spoke to Rachel.
Jacob said, “I am not God.”
Jacob said, “God has kept you from having children.”
passages.original: וַיִּֽחַר־ אַ֥ף יַעֲקֹ֖ב בְּרָחֵ֑ל וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הֲתַ֤חַת אֱלֹהִים֙ אָנֹ֔כִי אֲשֶׁר־ מָנַ֥ע מִמֵּ֖ךְ פְּרִי־ בָֽטֶן׃

passages.text: Then she said, “Here is my maidservant Bilhah. Sleep with her, that she may bear children for me, so that through her I too can build a family.”
passages.sermon:
Rachel could not have children for Jacob.
Rachel envied her sister.
Rachel spoke to Jacob.
Rachel said, “Here is my servant Bilhah.”
Rachel told Jacob, “Sleep with Bilhah.”
Rachel said, “Bilhah will bear children for me.”
Rachel said, “Through Bilhah, I also can have a family.”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֕אמֶר הִנֵּ֛ה אֲמָתִ֥י בִלְהָ֖ה בֹּ֣א אֵלֶ֑יהָ וְתֵלֵד֙ עַל־ בִּרְכַּ֔י וְאִבָּנֶ֥ה גַם־ אָנֹכִ֖י מִמֶּֽנָּה׃

passages.text: So Rachel gave Jacob her servant Bilhah as a wife, and he slept with her, and Bilhah conceived and bore him a son.
passages.sermon:
Rachel could not have children.
Rachel had a servant named Bilhah.
Rachel gave Bilhah to Jacob as a wife.
Jacob slept with Bilhah.
Bilhah became pregnant.
Bilhah gave birth to a son for Jacob.
passages.original: וַתִּתֶּן־ ל֛וֹ אֶת־ בִּלְהָ֥ה שִׁפְחָתָ֖הּ לְאִשָּׁ֑ה וַיָּבֹ֥א אֵלֶ֖יהָ יַעֲקֹֽב׃ וַתַּ֣הַר בִּלְהָ֔ה וַתֵּ֥לֶד לְיַעֲקֹ֖ב בֵּֽן׃

passages.text: Then Rachel said, “God has vindicated me; He has heard my plea and given me a son.” So she named him Dan.
passages.sermon:
Rachel was the wife of Jacob.
Rachel could not have children.
Rachel gave her servant Bilhah to Jacob as a wife.
Bilhah gave birth to a son for Jacob.
Rachel spoke about this son.
Rachel said, “God has judged my case.”
Rachel said, “God has listened to my voice.”
Rachel said, “God has given me a son.”
Rachel named the boy Dan.
passages.original: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר רָחֵל֙ דָּנַ֣נִּי אֱלֹהִ֔ים וְגַם֙ שָׁמַ֣ע בְּקֹלִ֔י וַיִּתֶּן־ לִ֖י בֵּ֑ן עַל־ כֵּ֛ן קָרְאָ֥ה שְׁמ֖וֹ דָּֽן׃

passages.text: And Rachel’s servant Bilhah conceived again and bore Jacob a second son.
passages.sermon:
Rachel had a servant named Bilhah.
Bilhah was Rachel’s servant.
Bilhah became pregnant again.
Bilhah gave birth to a second son for Jacob.
passages.original: וַתַּ֣הַר ע֔וֹד וַתֵּ֕לֶד בִּלְהָ֖ה שִׁפְחַ֣ת רָחֵ֑ל בֵּ֥ן שֵׁנִ֖י לְיַעֲקֹֽב׃

passages.text: Then Rachel said, “In my great struggles, I have wrestled with my sister and won.” So she named him Naphtali.
passages.sermon:
Rachel was the wife of Jacob.
Rachel could not have children for a long time.
Rachel gave her servant Bilhah to Jacob as a wife.
Bilhah bore Jacob a second son.
Rachel spoke about her feelings.
Rachel said she struggled greatly with her sister Leah.
Rachel said she wrestled with her sister and prevailed.
Rachel named the son Naphtali.
passages.original: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר רָחֵ֗ל נַפְתּוּלֵ֨י אֱלֹהִ֧ים׀ נִפְתַּ֛לְתִּי עִם־ אֲחֹתִ֖י גַּם־ יָכֹ֑לְתִּי וַתִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ נַפְתָּלִֽי׃

passages.text: When Leah saw that she had stopped having children, she gave her servant Zilpah to Jacob as a wife.
passages.sermon:
Leah was the wife of Jacob.
Leah saw that she had stopped having children.
Leah had a servant named Zilpah.
Leah took Zilpah.
Leah gave Zilpah to Jacob.
Leah gave Zilpah to Jacob as a wife.
passages.original: וַתֵּ֣רֶא לֵאָ֔ה כִּ֥י עָמְדָ֖ה מִלֶּ֑דֶת וַתִּקַּח֙ אֶת־ זִלְפָּ֣ה שִׁפְחָתָ֔הּ וַתִּתֵּ֥ן אֹתָ֛הּ לְיַעֲקֹ֖ב לְאִשָּֽׁה׃

passages.text: And Leah’s servant Zilpah bore Jacob a son.
passages.sermon:
Leah had a servant named Zilpah.
Zilpah was Leah’s maid.
Jacob was Leah’s husband.
Zilpah gave birth to a son.
Zilpah bore this son for Jacob.
passages.original: וַתֵּ֗לֶד זִלְפָּ֛ה שִׁפְחַ֥ת לֵאָ֖ה לְיַעֲקֹ֥ב בֵּֽן׃

passages.text: Then Leah said, “How fortunate!” So she named him Gad.
passages.sermon:
Leah was the wife of Jacob.
Leah saw that her servant Zilpah gave birth to a son for Jacob.
Leah said, "How fortunate!"
Leah named the boy Gad.
passages.original: וַתֹּ֥אמֶר לֵאָ֖ה בְּגָד וַתִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־ שְׁמ֖וֹ גָּֽד׃

passages.text: When Leah’s servant Zilpah bore Jacob a second son, Leah said, “How happy I am! For the women call me happy.” So she named him Asher.
passages.sermon:
Leah had a servant named Zilpah.
Zilpah was Leah’s servant.
Jacob was Leah’s husband.
Zilpah gave birth to a second son for Jacob.
Leah spoke about this event.
Leah said she was happy.
Leah said, “The women call me happy.”
Leah named the boy Asher.
passages.original: וַתֵּ֗לֶד זִלְפָּה֙ שִׁפְחַ֣ת לֵאָ֔ה בֵּ֥ן שֵׁנִ֖י לְיַעֲקֹֽב׃ וַתֹּ֣אמֶר לֵאָ֔ה בְּאָשְׁרִ֕י כִּ֥י אִשְּׁר֖וּנִי בָּנ֑וֹת וַתִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־ שְׁמ֖וֹ אָשֵֽׁר׃

passages.text: Now during the wheat harvest, Reuben went out and found some mandrakes in the field. When he brought them to his mother, Rachel begged Leah, “Please give me some of your son’s mandrakes.”
passages.sermon:
Reuben was Leah’s son.
It was the time of the wheat harvest.
Reuben went out into the field.
He found some mandrakes there.
He brought the mandrakes to his mother Leah.
Rachel saw this.
Rachel spoke to Leah.
Rachel said, “Please give me some of your son’s mandrakes.”
passages.original: וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ רְאוּבֵ֜ן בִּימֵ֣י קְצִיר־ חִטִּ֗ים וַיִּמְצָ֤א דֽוּדָאִים֙ בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה וַיָּבֵ֣א אֹתָ֔ם אֶל־ לֵאָ֖ה אִמּ֑וֹ וַתֹּ֤אמֶר רָחֵל֙ אֶל־ לֵאָ֔ה תְּנִי־ נָ֣א לִ֔י מִדּוּדָאֵ֖י בְּנֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: But Leah replied, “Is it not enough that you have taken away my husband? Now you want to take my son’s mandrakes as well?” “Very well,” said Rachel, “he may sleep with you tonight in exchange for your son’s mandrakes.”
passages.sermon:
Leah was Jacob’s wife.
Rachel was also Jacob’s wife.
Leah spoke to Rachel.
Leah said, “You have taken my husband.”
Leah said, “Is that not enough?”
Leah said, “Now you want to take my son’s mandrakes too.”
Rachel answered Leah.
Rachel said, “Very well.”
Rachel said, “Jacob may sleep with you tonight.”
Rachel said, “This is in exchange for your son’s mandrakes.”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר לָ֗הּ הַמְעַט֙ קַחְתֵּ֣ךְ אֶת־ אִישִׁ֔י וְלָקַ֕חַת גַּ֥ם אֶת־ דּוּדָאֵ֖י בְּנִ֑י וַתֹּ֣אמֶר רָחֵ֗ל לָכֵן֙ יִשְׁכַּ֤ב עִמָּךְ֙ הַלַּ֔יְלָה תַּ֖חַת דּוּדָאֵ֥י בְנֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: When Jacob came in from the field that evening, Leah went out to meet him and said, “You must come with me, for I have hired you with my son’s mandrakes.” So he slept with her that night.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was Leah’s husband.
Jacob came in from the field in the evening.
Leah went out to meet Jacob.
Leah spoke to Jacob.
Leah said, “You must come with me.”
Leah said, “I have hired you with my son’s mandrakes.”
Jacob slept with Leah that night.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֨א יַעֲקֹ֣ב מִן־ הַשָּׂדֶה֮ בָּעֶרֶב֒ וַתֵּצֵ֨א לֵאָ֜ה לִקְרָאת֗וֹ וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֵלַ֣י תָּב֔וֹא כִּ֚י שָׂכֹ֣ר שְׂכַרְתִּ֔יךָ בְּדוּדָאֵ֖י בְּנִ֑י וַיִּשְׁכַּ֥ב עִמָּ֖הּ בַּלַּ֥יְלָה הֽוּא׃

passages.text: And God listened to Leah, and she conceived and bore a fifth son to Jacob.
passages.sermon:
God listened to Leah.
Leah was Jacob’s wife.
Leah wanted children.
God answered Leah’s prayer.
Leah became pregnant.
Leah gave birth to a son.
This was Jacob’s fifth son from Leah.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמַ֥ע אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶל־ לֵאָ֑ה וַתַּ֛הַר וַתֵּ֥לֶד לְיַעֲקֹ֖ב בֵּ֥ן חֲמִישִֽׁי׃

passages.text: Then Leah said, “God has rewarded me for giving my maidservant to my husband.” So she named him Issachar.
passages.sermon:
Leah was Jacob’s wife.
Leah spoke.
Leah said, “God has rewarded me.”
Leah gave her maidservant to her husband Jacob.
Leah believed this act brought her God’s reward.
Leah named her son Issachar.
passages.original: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר לֵאָ֗ה נָתַ֤ן אֱלֹהִים֙ שְׂכָרִ֔י אֲשֶׁר־ נָתַ֥תִּי שִׁפְחָתִ֖י לְאִישִׁ֑י וַתִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ יִשָּׂשכָֽר׃

passages.text: Again Leah conceived and bore a sixth son to Jacob.
passages.sermon:
Leah was Jacob’s wife.
Leah conceived again.
Leah gave birth to a son.
This was the sixth son Leah bore to Jacob.
passages.original: וַתַּ֤הַר עוֹד֙ לֵאָ֔ה וַתֵּ֥לֶד בֵּן־ שִׁשִּׁ֖י לְּיַעֲקֹֽב׃

passages.text: “God has given me a good gift,” she said. “This time my husband will honor me, because I have borne him six sons.” And she named him Zebulun.
passages.sermon:
Leah was Jacob’s wife.
Leah spoke.
She said, “God has given me a good gift.”
She said, “Now my husband will honor me.”
She said this because she had given birth to six sons for Jacob.
Leah named the son Zebulun.
passages.original: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר לֵאָ֗ה זְבָדַ֨נִי אֱלֹהִ֥ים׀ אֹתִי֮ זֵ֣בֶד טוֹב֒ הַפַּ֙עַם֙ יִזְבְּלֵ֣נִי אִישִׁ֔י כִּֽי־ יָלַ֥דְתִּי ל֖וֹ שִׁשָּׁ֣ה בָנִ֑ים וַתִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־ שְׁמ֖וֹ זְבֻלֽוּן׃

passages.text: After that, Leah gave birth to a daughter and named her Dinah.
passages.sermon: Leah was Jacob’s wife.\r\nLeah gave birth to a daughter.\r\nLeah named her daughter Dinah.
passages.original: וְאַחַ֖ר יָ֣לְדָה בַּ֑ת וַתִּקְרָ֥א אֶת־ שְׁמָ֖הּ דִּינָֽה׃

passages.text: Then God remembered Rachel. He listened to her and opened her womb, and she conceived and gave birth to a son. “God has taken away my shame,” she said.
passages.sermon:
God remembered Rachel.
God listened to Rachel.
God opened Rachel’s womb.
Rachel conceived.
Rachel gave birth to a son.
Rachel said, “God has taken away my shame.”
passages.original: וַיִּזְכֹּ֥ר אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶת־ רָחֵ֑ל וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע אֵלֶ֙יהָ֙ אֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיִּפְתַּ֖ח אֶת־ רַחְמָֽהּ׃ וַתַּ֖הַר וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֑ן וַתֹּ֕אמֶר אָסַ֥ף אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶת־ חֶרְפָּתִֽי׃

passages.text: She named him Joseph, and said, “May the LORD add to me another son.”
passages.sermon: Rachel gave birth to a son.\r\nShe named him Joseph.\r\nShe said, “May the LORD add to me another son.”
passages.original: וַתִּקְרָ֧א אֶת־ שְׁמ֛וֹ יוֹסֵ֖ף לֵאמֹ֑ר יֹסֵ֧ף יְהוָ֛ה לִ֖י בֵּ֥ן אַחֵֽר׃

passages.text: Now after Rachel had given birth to Joseph, Jacob said to Laban, “Send me on my way so I can return to my homeland.
passages.sermon:
Rachel gave birth to Joseph.
Jacob was her husband.
Laban was Jacob’s father-in-law.
Jacob spoke to Laban.
Jacob said, “Send me away.”
Jacob wanted to return to his own home.
Jacob wanted to go back to his own land.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֕י כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר יָלְדָ֥ה רָחֵ֖ל אֶת־ יוֹסֵ֑ף וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יַעֲקֹב֙ אֶל־ לָבָ֔ן שַׁלְּחֵ֙נִי֙ וְאֵ֣לְכָ֔ה אֶל־ מְקוֹמִ֖י וּלְאַרְצִֽי׃

passages.text: Give me my wives and children for whom I have served you, that I may go on my way. You know how hard I have worked for you.”
passages.sermon:
Jacob spoke to Laban.
Jacob had served Laban for many years.
Jacob had worked to earn his wives and children.
Jacob said, “Give me my wives and my children.
I have served you for them.
Let me go on my way.
You know how I have worked for you.”
passages.original: תְּנָ֞ה אֶת־ נָשַׁ֣י וְאֶת־ יְלָדַ֗י אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָבַ֧דְתִּי אֹֽתְךָ֛ בָּהֵ֖ן וְאֵלֵ֑כָה כִּ֚י אַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֔עְתָּ אֶת־ עֲבֹדָתִ֖י אֲשֶׁ֥ר עֲבַדְתִּֽיךָ׃

passages.text: But Laban replied, “If I have found favor in your eyes, please stay. I have learned by divination that the LORD has blessed me because of you.”
passages.sermon:
Laban was Jacob’s father-in-law.
Laban spoke to Jacob.
Laban said, “If I have found favor in your eyes, please stay.”
Laban said, “I have learned by divination.”
Laban said, “The LORD has blessed me because of you.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ לָבָ֔ן אִם־ נָ֛א מָצָ֥אתִי חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֶ֑יךָ נִחַ֕שְׁתִּי וַיְבָרֲכֵ֥נִי יְהוָ֖ה בִּגְלָלֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: And he added, “Name your wages, and I will pay them.”
passages.sermon: Laban spoke to Jacob.\r\nLaban said, “Tell me what you want as your wages.\r\nI will pay you what you ask.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמַ֑ר נָקְבָ֧ה שְׂכָרְךָ֛ עָלַ֖י וְאֶתֵּֽנָה׃

passages.text: Then Jacob answered, “You know how I have served you and how your livestock have thrived under my care.
passages.sermon:
Jacob spoke to Laban.
Jacob said, “You know how I have worked for you.
You know how I have served you faithfully.
You also know what happened to your livestock when I was with you.
Your livestock did well under my care.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו אַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֔עְתָּ אֵ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֣ר עֲבַדְתִּ֑יךָ וְאֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־ הָיָ֥ה מִקְנְךָ֖ אִתִּֽי׃

passages.text: Indeed, you had very little before my arrival, but now your wealth has increased many times over. The LORD has blessed you wherever I set foot. But now, when may I also provide for my own household?”
passages.sermon:
Jacob spoke to Laban.
Jacob had worked for Laban for many years.
Before Jacob arrived, Laban had very little.
After Jacob came, Laban’s wealth grew greatly.
The LORD blessed Laban because of Jacob.
The LORD caused Laban to prosper wherever Jacob went.
Jacob then asked a question.
Jacob said, “When can I also provide for my own household?”
passages.original: כִּ֡י מְעַט֩ אֲשֶׁר־ הָיָ֨ה לְךָ֤ לְפָנַי֙ וַיִּפְרֹ֣ץ לָרֹ֔ב וַיְבָ֧רֶךְ יְהוָ֛ה אֹתְךָ֖ לְרַגְלִ֑י וְעַתָּ֗ה מָתַ֛י אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֥ה גַם־ אָנֹכִ֖י לְבֵיתִֽי׃

passages.text: “What can I give you?” Laban asked. “You do not need to give me anything,” Jacob replied. “If you do this one thing for me, I will keep on shepherding and keeping your flocks.
passages.sermon:
Laban spoke to Jacob.
Laban asked, “What can I give you?”
Jacob answered Laban.
Jacob said, “You do not need to give me anything.”
Jacob continued, “If you do this one thing for me, I will continue to shepherd your flocks.”
Jacob said, “I will keep and watch over your sheep.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר מָ֣ה אֶתֶּן־ לָ֑ךְ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יַעֲקֹב֙ לֹא־ תִתֶּן־ לִ֣י מְא֔וּמָה אִם־ תַּֽעֲשֶׂה־ לִּי֙ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה אָשׁ֛וּבָה אֶרְעֶ֥ה צֹֽאנְךָ֖ אֶשְׁמֹֽר׃

passages.text: Let me go through all your flocks today and remove from them every speckled or spotted sheep, every dark-colored lamb, and every spotted or speckled goat. These will be my wages.
passages.sermon:
Jacob spoke to Laban.
Jacob said, “Let me go through all your flocks today.
I will remove every sheep that is speckled or spotted.
I will remove every lamb that is dark-colored among the sheep.
I will remove every goat that is spotted or speckled.
These animals will be my wages.”
passages.original: אֶֽעֱבֹ֨ר בְּכָל־ צֹֽאנְךָ֜ הַיּ֗וֹם הָסֵ֨ר מִשָּׁ֜ם כָּל־ שֶׂ֣ה׀ נָקֹ֣ד וְטָל֗וּא וְכָל־ שֶׂה־ חוּם֙ בַּכְּשָׂבִ֔ים וְטָל֥וּא וְנָקֹ֖ד בָּעִזִּ֑ים וְהָיָ֖ה שְׂכָרִֽי׃

passages.text: So my honesty will testify for me when you come to check on my wages in the future. If I have any goats that are not speckled or spotted, or any lambs that are not dark-colored, they will be considered stolen.”
passages.sermon:
Jacob spoke to Laban.
Jacob wanted to show he was honest.
Jacob said his honesty would prove itself in the future.
Laban would come later to check Jacob’s wages.
Jacob said, “If you find any goat with me that is not speckled or spotted, it is stolen.”
Jacob also said, “If you find any lamb with me that is not dark-colored, it is stolen.”
passages.original: וְעָֽנְתָה־ בִּ֤י צִדְקָתִי֙ בְּי֣וֹם מָחָ֔ר כִּֽי־ תָב֥וֹא עַל־ שְׂכָרִ֖י לְפָנֶ֑יךָ כֹּ֣ל אֲשֶׁר־ אֵינֶנּוּ֩ נָקֹ֨ד וְטָל֜וּא בָּֽעִזִּ֗ים וְחוּם֙ בַּכְּשָׂבִ֔ים גָּנ֥וּב ה֖וּא אִתִּֽי׃

passages.text: “Agreed,” said Laban. “Let it be as you have said.”
passages.sermon:
Laban was Jacob’s employer and relative.
Laban listened to Jacob’s proposal.
Laban agreed to Jacob’s terms.
Laban said, “Let it be as you have said.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לָבָ֖ן הֵ֑ן ל֖וּ יְהִ֥י כִדְבָרֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: That very day Laban removed all the streaked or spotted male goats and every speckled or spotted female goat—every one that had any white on it—and every dark-colored lamb, and he placed them under the care of his sons.
passages.sermon:
Laban was Jacob’s father-in-law.
Laban acted on the same day.
Laban removed all the male goats that were streaked or spotted.
Laban removed all the female goats that were speckled or spotted.
Laban removed every goat that had any white on it.
Laban removed every lamb that was dark-colored.
Laban gave all these animals to his sons to take care of.
passages.original: וַיָּ֣סַר בַּיּוֹם֩ הַה֨וּא אֶת־ הַתְּיָשִׁ֜ים הָֽעֲקֻדִּ֣ים וְהַטְּלֻאִ֗ים וְאֵ֤ת כָּל־ הָֽעִזִּים֙ הַנְּקֻדּ֣וֹת וְהַטְּלֻאֹ֔ת כֹּ֤ל אֲשֶׁר־ לָבָן֙ בּ֔וֹ וְכָל־ ח֖וּם בַּכְּשָׂבִ֑ים וַיִּתֵּ֖ן בְּיַד־ בָּנָֽיו׃

passages.text: Then he put a three-day journey between himself and Jacob, while Jacob was shepherding the rest of Laban’s flocks.
passages.sermon:
Laban was the uncle and employer of Jacob.
Laban separated himself from Jacob.
Laban put a distance of three days’ journey between himself and Jacob.
Jacob stayed behind.
Jacob took care of the rest of Laban’s flocks.
passages.original: וַיָּ֗שֶׂם דֶּ֚רֶךְ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֔ים בֵּינ֖וֹ וּבֵ֣ין יַעֲקֹ֑ב וְיַעֲקֹ֗ב רֹעֶ֛ה אֶת־ צֹ֥אן לָבָ֖ן הַנּוֹתָרֹֽת׃

passages.text: Jacob, however, took fresh branches of poplar, almond, and plane trees, and peeled the bark, exposing the white inner wood of the branches.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was a shepherd.
Jacob took fresh branches.
He chose branches from poplar trees.
He chose branches from almond trees.
He chose branches from plane trees.
Jacob peeled the bark from the branches.
He exposed the white inner wood on the branches.
passages.original: וַיִּֽקַּֽח־ ל֣וֹ יַעֲקֹ֗ב מַקַּ֥ל לִבְנֶ֛ה לַ֖ח וְל֣וּז וְעֶרְמ֑וֹן וַיְפַצֵּ֤ל בָּהֵן֙ פְּצָל֣וֹת לְבָנ֔וֹת מַחְשֹׂף֙ הַלָּבָ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־ הַמַּקְלֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Then he set the peeled branches in the watering troughs in front of the flocks coming in to drink. So when the flocks were in heat and came to drink, they mated in front of the branches. And they bore young that were streaked or speckled or spotted.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was a shepherd.
Jacob took branches and peeled them.
He put the peeled branches in the watering troughs.
The watering troughs were where the flocks came to drink.
He placed the branches in front of the flocks.
The flocks came to drink water.
The flocks were in heat when they came to drink.
The flocks mated in front of the branches.
The flocks gave birth to young.
The young were streaked.
The young were speckled.
The young were spotted.
passages.original: וַיַּצֵּ֗ג אֶת־ הַמַּקְלוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר פִּצֵּ֔ל בָּרֳהָטִ֖ים בְּשִֽׁקֲת֣וֹת הַמָּ֑יִם אֲשֶׁר֩ תָּבֹ֨אןָ הַצֹּ֤אן לִשְׁתּוֹת֙ לְנֹ֣כַח הַצֹּ֔אן וַיֵּחַ֖מְנָה בְּבֹאָ֥ן לִשְׁתּֽוֹת׃ וַיֶּחֱמ֥וּ הַצֹּ֖אן אֶל־ הַמַּקְל֑וֹת וַתֵּלַ֣דְןָ הַצֹּ֔אן עֲקֻדִּ֥ים נְקֻדִּ֖ים וּטְלֻאִֽים׃

passages.text: Jacob set apart the young, but made the rest face the streaked dark-colored sheep in Laban’s flocks. Then he set his own stock apart and did not put them with Laban’s animals.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the son of Isaac and the grandson of Abraham.
Jacob worked for Laban, his father-in-law.
Jacob separated the young animals from the flock.
Jacob made the rest of the animals face the streaked and dark-colored sheep in Laban’s flock.
Jacob set his own animals apart from the others.
Jacob did not put his animals with Laban’s animals.
passages.original: וְהַכְּשָׂבִים֮ הִפְרִ֣יד יַעֲקֹב֒ וַ֠יִּתֵּן פְּנֵ֨י הַצֹּ֧אן אֶל־ עָקֹ֛ד וְכָל־ ח֖וּם בְּצֹ֣אן לָבָ֑ן וַיָּֽשֶׁת־ ל֤וֹ עֲדָרִים֙ לְבַדּ֔וֹ וְלֹ֥א שָׁתָ֖ם עַל־ צֹ֥אן לָבָֽן׃

passages.text: Whenever the stronger females of the flock were in heat, Jacob would place the branches in the troughs, in full view of the animals, so that they would breed in front of the branches.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was a shepherd.
Jacob cared for Laban’s flocks.
Some female sheep in the flock were strong.
When these strong females were in heat, Jacob acted.
Jacob took branches.
Jacob placed the branches in the watering troughs.
Jacob put the branches where the sheep could see them.
The strong female sheep came to the troughs.
The strong female sheep mated in front of the branches.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֗ה בְּכָל־ יַחֵם֮ הַצֹּ֣אן הַמְקֻשָּׁרוֹת֒ וְשָׂ֨ם יַעֲקֹ֧ב אֶת־ הַמַּקְל֛וֹת לְעֵינֵ֥י הַצֹּ֖אן בָּרֳהָטִ֑ים לְיַחְמֵ֖נָּה בַּמַּקְלֽוֹת׃

passages.text: But if the animals were weak, he did not set out the branches. So the weaker animals went to Laban and the stronger ones to Jacob.
passages.sermon:
Jacob worked for Laban.
Jacob separated his own flocks from Laban’s flocks.
When the animals were weak, Jacob did not put the branches in front of them.
The weak animals became Laban’s.
The strong animals became Jacob’s.
passages.original: וּבְהַעֲטִ֥יף הַצֹּ֖אן לֹ֣א יָשִׂ֑ים וְהָיָ֤ה הָעֲטֻפִים֙ לְלָבָ֔ן וְהַקְּשֻׁרִ֖ים לְיַעֲקֹֽב׃

passages.text: Thus Jacob became exceedingly prosperous. He owned large flocks, maidservants and menservants, and camels and donkeys.
passages.sermon:
Jacob became very prosperous.
He gained many flocks.
He owned many female servants.
He owned many male servants.
He had camels.
He had donkeys.
passages.original: וַיִּפְרֹ֥ץ הָאִ֖ישׁ מְאֹ֣ד מְאֹ֑ד וַֽיְהִי־ לוֹ֙ צֹ֣אן רַבּ֔וֹת וּשְׁפָחוֹת֙ וַעֲבָדִ֔ים וּגְמַלִּ֖ים וַחֲמֹרִֽים׃
